name: Shackleton Rim
profile: Near-continuous grazing sunlight on rim; borders deep PSR ice trap

name: Peak Near Shackleton
profile: High-altitude illumination peak; steep surrounding terrain
targetHighlight: Severe slope landing hazard; exceptional solar line-of-sight

name: Connecting Ridge
profile: Narrow ridge between Shackleton and de Gerlache craters

name: de Gerlache Rim 2
profile: High solar illumination fraction; challenging Earth visibility
targetHighlight: Prolonged solar endurance; periodic S-Band horizon masking

name: Malapert Massif
profile: Elevated ridge with strong Direct-to-Earth line-of-sight
targetHighlight: Massif summit provides nearly 100% Earth visibility over lunar cycle

name: Mons Mouton Plateau
profile: Broad flat-topped massif; ideal for roving and solar masts
targetHighlight: Low slope terrain minimizes rover tip risk; favorable for drilling payload

name: Nobile Rim 1
profile: Prime water-ice reconnaissance target with seasonal shadows
targetHighlight: Close proximity to cold traps containing volatile deposits

name: Haworth Crater Rim
profile: Extreme thermal contrast adjacent to large permanent shadow zone
targetHighlight: Borders cryogenic depression with temperatures below 40 Kelvin

name: Leibnitz Beta Plateau
profile: High elevation plateau with strong Earth visibility
targetHighlight: Stable communications geometry with minimal multipath dropouts

name: Shiv Shakti Point
profile: Southern high-latitude plains benchmark (~14 Earth-day sunlight cycle)
targetHighlight: High-latitude landing baseline; standard day-night cycle with 14-day night

name: Sea of Tranquility
profile: Equatorial baseline for comparing terrestrial vs. polar lighting
targetHighlight: Equatorial benchmark: diurnal sun reaches 89° elevation; 354 hr continuous night

name: Von Karman Crater
profile: Lunar far-side benchmark (0% Direct-to-Earth visibility; requires relay)
targetHighlight: Far-side radio silence: 0% DTE visibility; strictly requires Queqiao relay
